current_runtime.f4_text: For long-running commands, run them in background and redirect output to a tmp file that you can read from later.

A_model_polling_only.notes: Current implementation. LIVE specimen proved the user's 'wait until finished' intent is not honored (model emitted done without polling). User-visible mismatch with the runtime promise.

B_opt_in_notify_on_terminal.notes: WAIT(v1) honestly collapses to NOTIFY semantics; strict WAIT (STRICT_WAIT) deferred to future cycle requiring Candidate C architecture. Adds one optional schema field (notifyOnCompletion). Default false preserves current behavior. Wake is one bounded generated prompt string delivered via PendingPromptsController exactly-once.

C_explicit_await_terminal.notes: Requires a new suspended-tool state machine. The runtime has no seam for suspended tool/turn ownership. Architecturally invasive. Not in v1 scope. Would enable STRICT_WAIT in a future cycle.

D_explicit_multi_mode.notes: Union of B and C. Without C's architecture, collapses to B with three mode labels.

contract.wait_v1: honestly collapses to NOTIFY semantics. Mapped to notifyOnCompletion:true. Strict WAIT (no Your turn interlude before final answer) is UNSUPPORTED in v1; deferred to STRICT_WAIT (future cycle requiring Candidate C architecture). User-facing doctrine states this explicitly.
contract.notify: notifyOnCompletion:true -> one wake at terminal via PendingPromptsController.enqueue. Wake prompt is a bounded generated prompt string (NOT typed payload); delivery='queue' by default; exactly-once.
contract.detach: notifyOnCompletion:false (default); no wake; current behavior preserved exactly.
contract.strict_wait_future: notifyOnCompletion:'wait'. Requires suspended-tool state machine (Candidate C). Tracked but NOT in v1 contract.
contract.wake_representation: bounded generated prompt string via formatTerminalWakePrompt(payload). Hard cap 8 KB; soft target 4 KB. Schema frozen in §15.7.2.
contract.wake_trigger: CommandJobManager.onCommandJobLifecycle event 'command_job_terminal_committed' (per-job, fires exactly once per terminal job). NOT the >0->0 cardinal transition.
contract.notification_identity_owner: session/coordinator-owned. Captured at run_commands call time at SdkSessionEventCoordinator seam (where options.getTask().taskId is reachable). Stored in per-session Map<jobId, {sessionId, taskId, epoch, notifyOnCompletion}>. NOT on CommandJob.
contract.multi_job_held_set: at session/coordinator seam; FIFO drain when the last notify=true job terminates.
contract.terminal_success: wake prompt content: 'Background command {jobId} exited successfully: code=0. stdoutTail: <tail>. stderrTail: <tail>. elapsedMs: {ms}.'
contract.terminal_failure: wake prompt content: 'Background command {jobId} exited with code {exitCode}. stdoutTail: <tail>. stderrTail: <tail>. elapsedMs: {ms}.'
contract.cancel: wake prompt content: 'Background command {jobId} was cancelled. stdoutTail: <tail>. stderrTail: <tail>. elapsedMs: {ms}.'
contract.deadline: wake prompt content: 'Background command {jobId} exceeded the host execution deadline and was terminated: code=null, signal=SIGKILL. stdoutTail: <tail>. stderrTail: <tail>. elapsedMs: {ms}.'
contract.spawn_failed: wake prompt content: 'Background command {jobId} failed to start: {error}. stdoutTail: <empty>. stderrTail: <empty>. elapsedMs: {ms}.'
contract.newer_turn: delivery='queue'; wake waits behind current turn; drain delivers after current turn's non-error finish.
contract.persistence: EPHEMERAL_ONLY for v1; wake lost on host restart; user-facing doctrine states this explicitly.

terminal_reason_matrix.containment_failed: UNSAFE_TO_DECLARE_TERMINAL -> NO wake (diagnostic only); wake consumer subscribes ONLY to command_job_terminal_committed, not containment_failed

upstream_divergence_record.rationale: Upstream's notifyParent default-true is one viable design; ClineMM v1 chooses default-false for backwards compatibility. notifyOnCompletion is host-builtin (not plugin) and reuses the existing PendingPromptsController.enqueue seam rather than the plugin host's steer_message.

verdict_basis: Contract B passes all ten rubric items D1-D10 WHEN D1 is read as D1a strict WAIT = NO/OUT_OF_V1 and D1b v1 WAIT(v1)→NOTIFY mapping = YES. B is the bounded v1 NOTIFY contract, not 'B fully implements literal WAIT'. Recon in §3-§6 establishes that the selected seams (PendingPromptsController.enqueue, identity-correlating machinery at coordinator seam, CommandJobManager.onCommandJobLifecycle command_job_terminal_committed event) all exist and are reusable. Default false preserves current behavior. WAIT(v1) honestly collapses to NOTIFY semantics; strict WAIT (STRICT_WAIT) deferred to future cycle requiring Candidate C architecture. Wake is bounded generated prompt string (NOT typed payload — PendingPromptsController accepts only prompt: string). Notification identity owner is session/coordinator-owned (CommandJob does not capture taskId). The COORDINATOR owns BOTH the identity map AND the active-notify set (post-CORRECTION02 §15.7.3); the wake consumer MUST NOT query CommandJobManager for notification semantics. Multi-job trigger is per-job terminal event (NOT >0->0 cardinal transition). NOTIFICATION_LIFETIME_INVARIANT (§10.8) governs the wake consumer: same sessionId + same taskId → KEEP; different sessionId OR different taskId → DISCARD; epoch is NOT used. Scenario suite S1-S11 fully defined. Successor ACT bounded and bound to this ACT's exit_head. CORRECTION02 closed all four defects from HALT_WAIT_SEMANTICS_STALE_CONTRACT_AUTHORITY.
